title: Your Five Senses
summary: See, hear, smell, taste and touch: how your body tells you about the world.

steps.title: Five helpers
sentences: You have five senses: sight, hearing, smell, taste and touch.
Each sense has its own body part: eyes, ears, nose, tongue and skin.
They send messages to your brain, and your brain tells you what is happening.

steps.title: Seeing and hearing
sentences: Your eyes catch light and your brain turns it into pictures.
Your ears catch sound waves, tiny shakes in the air, and your brain turns them into sounds.
Never poke anything into your ears or eyes, and keep loud sounds away from your ears.

steps.title: Smell and taste
sentences: Your nose can tell many different smells.
Your tongue can tell sweet, salty, sour, bitter and savoury tastes.
Smell and taste work together, and that is why food seems to have no taste when your nose is blocked.

steps.title: Touch
sentences: Your skin can feel hot, cold, soft, rough, and pain.
It feels pain to warn you when something might hurt you.
The skin is the largest organ of your body.

facts: Fingertips are one of the most sensitive parts of the body.
A dog's sense of smell is far stronger than ours.
Your tongue has thousands of tiny taste buds.

quiz.q: Which sense do you use to feel something soft?
How many senses do we usually talk about?
quiz.why: Sight, hearing, smell, taste and touch.
